notes: On my phone it looks clean and calm and the text is easy to read. The short-answer cards are big and clear, the coloured labels are explained once and are easy to follow, and the red 'Can you afford to be wrong?' box with its bar draws exactly my worry (report-phone.png; report.txt:401-408). The slider chart with 'Break-even: 9' and 'Why this changed' worked for me (report.txt:454-489). Nothing spills off the side at 390 px. But the report runs to about 28 phone screens (report-phone.png is 23,943 px tall). Step 2 alone is about four screens of 17 cards, each with 'Why it matters' and one or two chips (report.txt:106-226). Between customers I would lose my place there. In the outcomes chart the dashed worst-case line runs through 'Cautious|3 a day' and the minus of '−€371'. The round-by-round grid cuts its headers short ('Launch day: the board..', 'First week, Tuesday...') and is mostly 'Not around'. 'Check these with real customers' wears the blue 'Your number' chip (report.txt:792-794). The landing promises seven steps; the report has six. The connect page is code blocks, mcp.json and terminal commands that break mid-word ('api/m' / 'cp'). Nothing on it is for me (connect-phone.png).
improvements: Report, Step 2 'Your numbers' on phone (report.txt:102-226, about 4 screens in report-phone.png): 13 fact and plan cards each repeat 'Why it matters' plus a 'Demo data' chip before any result. Show 'Facts about your café' and 'Your plan' as one compact two-column list (label, value), closed behind 'See all 13 numbers'. Keep 'Guesses nobody knows yet' open, because the page says those drive the result. Criterion: one idea per step, phone reading between customers. It worked when Step 3 'Possible outcomes' starts within about 5 phone screens of the top instead of about 7.5.

Connect page and the landing's 'Add What-IF to your AI' (connect-phone.png; landing.txt:150-204): the first words are 'an MCP server', then the URL box and code blocks (mcp.json, a terminal command that wraps as 'api/m' / 'cp'). Put one owner card first: 'Use it in Claude or ChatGPT: 4 taps, about 2 minutes', with a picture of where Settings → Connectors is. Fold Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and 'Any other MCP client' under 'For developers'. Criterion: a non-technical helper connected in two minutes. It worked when the first phone screen of /connect has no code, no 'MCP' without a plain word beside it, and one button.

Report, Step 3 chart 'Result over the 10-day test' at 390 px: the dashed 'Worst case −€560' line crosses the row labels ('Cautious|3 a day', 'Expected|8 a day', 'Optimistic|15 a day') and the minus sign of '−€371'. Put the scenario labels on their own line above each bar, or start the bars right of the label column so the dashed line never crosses text. It worked when a zoom on report-phone.png shows no line through any label or value.

Report, Step 5 'What each one did, round by round' on phone: the column headers are cut ('Launch day: the board..', 'First week, Tuesday...'), and 11 of the 24 squares say 'Not around' in dashed grey, so the grid looks empty. Derya is 'Not around' in all four rounds. On phone, show the round names in full in a short legend above the grid ('R1 = launch day, board goes up'), shade the 'Not around' squares lighter, and drop or explain a customer who is never around. The 'Fan' badge on Felix, who has 'never been in', should say what it rates ('Mood about the deal: keen'). It worked when Selin can read every header and the grid's two coloured states without tapping.

Report labels and step counts: 'Check these with real customers' carries the blue 'Your number' chip (report.txt:792-794), but it is a to-do list, not my number. Remove the chip or use a neutral 'To do' style. The landing says 'Seven small steps' and 'Step 1 of 7' (landing.txt:37, 42), while the report says 'Step 6/6' (report.txt:15). Make both say six steps plus 'come back after the test'. Also show '−€56' rather than '−€56.02' on the headline cards, matching every other whole-euro figure. It worked when no chip on report-phone.png contradicts the legend in Step 2, and the step counts match.
understood: The three short-answer cards at the top: 9 a day needed, −€56 on my likely guess, −€560 at worst (37% of my spare cash).
Blue = my number, yellow = a guess, grey = calculated, pink = imagined, green = demo. The box in Step 2 explains it once and the chips repeat it everywhere.
The slider chart: green above zero makes money, red below loses, and the line crosses at 9.
The red bar in 'Can you afford to be wrong?': 37% used, 63% left.
The longest bar in 'Which guess matters most' is the one to test: extra customers a day.
The test card prints, and keep / tweak / stop are in green, yellow and red boxes with words, not only colours.
confused: Step 2 is a long run of cards that all look the same, each with 'Why it matters' and 'Demo data' (report.txt:106-226)
The dashed worst-case line running through 'Cautious|3 a day' and '−|€371' in the outcomes chart
Cut-off grid headers 'Launch day: the board..' and 'First week, Tuesday...' in the rehearsal grid
'Check these with real customers' tagged 'Your number' (report.txt:792-794)
Connect page: 'MCP server', 'mcp.json', 'Streamable HTTP transport', and code that breaks as 'api/m' / 'cp' (connect-phone.png)
Felix's green 'Fan' badge next to 'never been in' (report.txt:572, 578)
wouldTry: maybe, because I could follow the report on my phone and would print the test card. But the report is too long to finish between customers, and the 'Add to your AI' page is written for someone who uses a terminal. I would not get my own numbers in without help.
learnedAboutAI: The coloured labels taught me the difference: grey 'Calculated' is plain arithmetic I can open and check, yellow 'A guess' is something nobody knows yet, and pink 'Imagined' is made-up customers who are never counted in the money. The 'It can / It cannot' box made that clear. But two boxes next to each other say both 'played by an AI' and 'no AI', so I can't tell what the AI did here.
